title: Apiary management
competency: Choose and manage a good apiary site.

keywords.def: Caring for an apiary, starting with a good site for the hives.
Plants that bees visit for nectar and pollen.
A hedge or wall that protects hives from strong wind.

en.text: Good apiary management starts with a good site. A poor site means people and animals may be stung; an insecure site means honey and hives can be stolen. The site should be easy to reach, fenced, away from homes and roads, shaded at midday, sheltered from wind, near clean water, rich in bee flora, and free from pollution, smoke and disease.

screens.title: Where to put hives
screens.ask: Where should you NOT place beehives?
opts: Next to a busy road and a school
In a fenced, quiet place near flowers
screens.after: Bees can sting. Keep hives away from people, animals and roads.

opts: It prevents stings and theft, meets the bees' needs and saves time and money
